definitions.explanation: A common Japanese surname, built from {藤|ふじ} (wisteria) + {井|い} (well), another combination typical of surnames descended from branches of the {藤原|ふじわら} clan.

examples.japanese: {藤井|ふじい}さんに⟦{電話|でんわ}→電話：01471_denwa⟧をかけた。
{藤井|ふじい}という{名字|みょうじ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{西日本|にしにほん}→西日本：27538_nishinihon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: The surname Fujii is common in western Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦クラス→クラス：01084_kurasu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{藤井|ふじい}さんが⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧いて、⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{間違|まちが}えられる→間違える：01109_machigaeru⟧。
examples.english: There are two Fujiis in my class, and people often mix them up.

notes:
{藤井|ふじい} pairs ⟦{藤|ふじ}→藤：04396_fuji⟧ (wisteria) with {井|い} (well), following the same naming pattern as ⟦{藤田|ふじた}→藤田：30976_fujita⟧ and other ⟦{藤|ふじ}→藤：04396_fuji⟧-based surnames.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Like other surnames built on ⟦{藤|ふじ}→藤：04396_fuji⟧, {藤井|ふじい} traces back to descendants and retainers of the {藤原|ふじわら} clan, who took surnames combining the ⟦{藤|ふじ}→藤：04396_fuji⟧ character with a place or landscape feature associated with their family.
